summary.en: The Bobcat Adventure is the first required Adventure on the trail to earn the Lion badge of rank. Once the Bobcat Adventure is completed, Lions can start any other of the Adventures in any order. Bobcat is focused on character and introducing the values of Scouting America.

The natural environment continues to be a great place to learn and discover. The value of being outdoors has been proven to have benefits for both youth and adults. For Lion Cub Scouts, this means simply taking a walk outside and noting what they see. Lions and adult partners will take a walk to explore the outdoors. Along the way, they will see and identify things that are natural and things that are man-made.

Personal fitness is learning about proper nutrition, hygiene, exercise, and rest. Children who develop habits at an early age are more likely to continue those habits into adulthood. In this Adventure, Lions will explore the different food groups, have fun being active, and learn about the importance of rest.

Citizenship is one of the four aims of the Scouting America program. For Lions, citizenship begins at home with those they live with. They will explore how they can contribute to their home and community. Citizenship is about actively participating with those around you to create a community. For Lion Cub Scouts, their community is their home and the people they live with. Learning that they, too, can contribute and have a part in their home is the objective of this Adventure.
In partnership with the Barbara Sinatra Children’s Center Foundation, Lions will learn about the Protect Yourself Rules and other skills needed to stay safe.

In this Adventure, the Lions learn about their family by exploring the faith traditions and celebrations that make being part of their family special. This Adventure is commonly done at home with the Cub Scout’s family. If it is being done as a den, ensure that every parent and guardian is aware of the content and the activities that the den will do, and allow for parents to opt out of doing it as a den activity and choose to complete the requirement at home. This Adventure may be earned by completing the requirements OR by completing a religious emblem of the Cub Scout’s family’s choosing.

body.en: This deck contains cards to help den leaders deliver a program to complete all requirements for earning the Lion rank. How to use this deck 1. Review the other resource cards (black border) in this deck, and review the contents. 2. Pick the Adventure you want to work on in your next den meeting. 3. Remove all cards associated with that Adventure. 4. Scan the Adventure card, and review the webpage for the Adventure you chose. Read and follow the Safety Moment for the Adventure. 5. Select one activity card for each requirement to do in your meeting. 6. Scan the QR code for each activity you selected, and follow the directions on the activity page. 7. When conducting your den meeting, have your cards on hand to use as a quick guide. Scan here for a video that shows you how to use this deck. ‣
